raw_response:
I farm only 9 mu, so I will keep the full wheat-maize rotation on all of it. With 30 years of experience and well irrigation, I will stay with the practices I trust most: I will use better seed, put most of my fertilizer into nitrogen with enough phosphorus and some potassium, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and keep field work simple because some family labor is away working off-farm. For wheat, I will aim for a steady stand, enough water at key stages, and moderate plant protection so I do not lose yield. After wheat harvest, I will plant maize on the same 9 mu and use hybrid seed because that is what I would rely on for stable production. I will use rotary tillage because it is faster and fits my labor situation. I am not chasing the very highest input level; I will choose a middle path that protects yield, controls cost, and matches what I can manage myself.
